item.title: Many Berkeley teachers spend over $500 of their own money on student basics. That’s just wrong
item.description: Tissues, books, shoes, snacks and maxi pads. A BUSD teacher surveyed 42 colleagues and found half spend more than $500 a year on everything from basic hygiene supplies to prom tickets.

item.title: Celebration of life for Betty Reid Soskin set for March 1
item.description: The beloved national park ranger, civil rights pioneer and co-founder of Reid’s Records in Berkeley died in December. She will be honored at the Kaiser Center for the Arts in Oakland.

item.title: With patties built on brisket, Tommy’s Burger Co. in Richmond pursues the perfect smash
item.description: Tommy Ryan's burger spot was born from a desire to make the most out of all the meat moving through his Hercules barbecue joint.

item.title: Friends gather at Starry Plough to remember musician Anthony ‘Ant’ Anderson, killed by county sheriff deputies Monday
item.description: People cried, hugged, and told stories punctuated with laughter while remembering the 40-year-old trumpet player who "brought people together." The state’s DA office is investigating the killing.

item.title: Berkeley Tesla stun gun defendant, shot in later standoff, is exonerated
item.description: While Ricardo G. Ruiz has been found not guilty for the Fourth Street fracas, he still faces 11 felony charges from the armed April 2025 standoff that ended after a Berkeley Police Department officer shot him in the face.

item.title: What’s next for police accountability in Berkeley?
item.description: The sudden ouster of Police Accountability Board director Hansel Aguilar, and recent protest resignations from the Police Accountability Board, are the culmination of years of mounting tension between those bodies and the city.

item.title: 3 ideas Cal students dreamed up to make life better in Berkeley
item.description: In a weeklong sprint, teams of UC Berkeley students invented solutions for city problems like disposing of furniture and making homes fire-safe. Then they pitched their ideas to Berkeley’s mayor and others.

item.title: ‘Air filled with danger’: What East Bay clergy witnessed in Minneapolis
item.description: Two Unitarian ministers joined 700 clergy who flew in from around the country to bear ‘faithful witness’ to ICE’s violent presence.

item.title: Grand Opening Bakery debuts with Lunar New Year specialities, and a new Berkeley provisions shop is almost ready
item.description: A running list of restaurants that have recently opened in Berkeley, Oakland, Richmond, and beyond.

item.title: Coastal flood advisory issued for area including Berkeley shoreline
item.description: Berkeley has received more than 2 inches of rain within the last 48 hours as Bay Area cities grapple with switch back to wintery weather.
